sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Sometimes it is good to reflect. You have to look back to see where you started so that you can truly appreciate where you are now, and it puts into perspective where we are going.

This truth did not look like this twenty years ago, in 2006; nowhere close. What will it look like in another twenty years, Lord's will? There are individuals sitting in the congregation now who are going to take this thing to a whole other level, but they have to be able to see themselves doing it.

The Bible is not a book that sits on the counter. We believe on it and we apply what we learn, knowing the things promised to us in the scriptures are going to come to pass, and so we keep striving and working hard so that the kingdom of heaven will come upon us. Later in the class the old pictures were shown for this very reason: to see the souls who endeavoured to keep the unity and are still striving, the ones who passed away in the truth, the ones who left, and how the few brothers grew into a congregation and a school.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Everyone who has been sitting in this truth should be able to explain it. When we are together and unified, there is nothing we cannot accomplish.

The unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this earth, to this evil world we presently live in. It scares the mess out of these folks.

If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the unity of the Hoovers, not the Omegas, the Kappas or the Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is not just some Negroes coming together. This unity is being unified in Christ, hence the name Israel United in Christ. To be united in the Lord is true unity.

precepts.why:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The unity of brethren in what? Righteousness. The love of neighbours is not an oogly googly feeling of friendship; it is unity in righteousness.

A man and a wife that agree together agree in righteousness. A sanctified, holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before him. The love of brethren is someone who shows care for his nation and his people.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Paul wrote to the congregations that were puffed up and full of schisms: that is not unity. To be unified is to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it and the way Christ told us to be.

To truly be unified we must be one in Christ: “That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. This is not us joining the Trinity. The Most High and his son are not the same person; as Christ is one with the Father, we have to be one with Christ.

“That the world may believe that thou hast sent me.” The whole world is waiting on the sanctification and unification of the nation of Israel. Once we come together and truly become one, this whole earth is going to get right. Bishop Yohoshua has been speaking on this level of unity and organisation for quite some time (the throwback video was ten years ago), because the Lord gave him the vision; the Lord has been pushing us this direction for a long time, and the only way it happens is if we are one in Christ.

“Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.” We have to strive to be unified. It takes work; it does not just happen. As we come together there will be issues with the brethren, and we have to know how to apply the scriptures to remain unified.

The work is being able to spot Satan when he comes through the door, because Satan is coming in to destroy unity, the very thing that is the biggest threat to this present world. In real time that is spotting those who bring in schisms and other doctrines, or put spirits on brothers and sisters, and calling them out, even kicking them out; bringing home the one drawing back; forgiving your brother when you are offended.

It is also having the testicular fortitude to look your good friend in the eye, the one you do not want a confrontation with, and because you love him, love this nation and this body, saying, Hold on, you got the damn devil on you. Did you speak to him to his face? Why are you telling all of us? When people are comfortable spreading things and not dealing with them the scriptural way, gossip and whispering and secrets become normal in the congregation.

“There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism”. Everything is unified, of the selfsame spirit, and we have to be the exact same way. If a brother or sister is going the wrong way or trying to gossip, they should hear the exact same response over and over from whoever they bring it to: you better fix yourself. That makes Satan work hard to get in here. When everybody is of the same mind, it cannot happen.

sense.text:
1 Corinthians 12 is the embodiment of what a body takes in order to function. We would not be where we are without understanding it, and there is still more brick to put in to go to the next level and do greater things.

Paul is addressing the body, writing to a congregation about its issues and educating it in the things of the Lord; imagine Paul writing to the Oklahomans. “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant.” Do not get high-minded with the gift you have. To understand the functioning of the body you have to realise what every individual is worth. Nobody is above this. You are special because you are part of the body, but do not think you are more than another part. We are the same people, all working toward the selfsame goal, and we have to do exactly what the Lord told us to do to get where we need to get.

There are so many offices in this body that it would blow your mind. You came in, got patted down, dropped your kids off and did not think twice about it; you will get a plate of food today with no idea how many hands made it possible. People have gifts to deal with things you never have to think about.

“Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” Paul leads with this before he goes over the gifts and members of the body. Were is past tense: they are not Gentiles any more. Gentile here is the Hellenized Jew. They were not used to the organisation of the Lord, to his laws and his order, because they had been Gentiles. The spirit of niggardom has been around a long time.

Why does it matter that they were carried away unto dumb idols? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or to sound doctrine, not accustomed to what he is about to go over. They had been following dumb idols, doing what others wanted instead of what the Most High God wanted. To show and teach organisation to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult, so Paul reminds them of the mind frame they came from, so they can appreciate where they are and go ten times harder: that ain't us no more; renew your mind; we do not conduct ourselves like that any longer.

“Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed”. If anybody is speaking by the spirit of God, would he say Christ is accursed? No. “And that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.” By him actions are weighed. In that day, someone who said Christ was accursed was not of the Lord, and someone who confessed Christ is Lord showed that he believed.

precepts.why:
“Be not ignorant of any thing in a great matter or a small.” Paul tells the Corinthians, I do not want you ignorant of this; you need to learn it and understand it. You have to understand the great matters as well as the small.

Do not be ignorant of the functionings of this body. It is easy to come in, sit down and think everybody is just doing what they do, but when you sit back and see how intricate this thing is, how many offices there are, from those who care for the children to those who prepare the food, you stop being ignorant of it.

“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think. The scriptures are supposed to be inside you now, and you have to apply them.

“That ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” To prove is to know a thing is what it is: you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now.

In the church we were ignorant, dumb as hell, just walking the line doing what everybody did: Christmas, birthdays, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, never asking why. Now it has to make sense: what does the scripture say, and where is that in the Bible? That is proving what is acceptable unto the Most High God.

What is the will of the Lord? “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God. To have them within your heart is to be able to process, to understand, to know and to see clearly.

You have understanding now: you bounce things off the scriptures, you no longer conform to this world, and you do not move like everybody else any more. You are using your mind for what it is for.

You have one job on this earth, and you have been given a mind to do it. “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments”. You have a brain to understand how to fear God, to understand what the commandments of God are, and to apply the laws of God in your life. That is the meaning of life.

If you use your mind for anything else, you missed it, and you are on the broad road to destruction. Fill your mind with thus saith the Lord, not Mortal Kombat moves, not Kobe's stats or the NBA finals. We do not give a damn about any of that. Apply your mind to what is necessary: how do I deal with my wife and my kids, and how can I become stronger and a better asset in this truth so the Lord can use me? If you are concerned with something else, maybe this ain't you.

“For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied. If your mind is filled with Mortal Kombat moves and the stats of the greatest to ever play, that is where your focus is and where you are building your treasure.

“Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. When you occupy your mind in the laws of God, that is where you lay your treasure, not on earth; the carnal things are going to be destroyed.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt”. Our minds should be occupied in the laws of God, in how to unify, how to be used as a tool in the Lord's army and how to push this truth further: treasure in heaven that cannot be corrupted.

This is how Gentiles in the flesh think. “Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” In that time people of our own people consented to the religion of the Greeks, which was idolatry. They gave up what God told them to do and did what the Greeks wanted them to do. This is Hellenization.

The king sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, forbid the offerings, made them “profane the sabbaths and festival days”, and “pollute the sanctuary and holy people”. They made it unlawful even to call yourself a Jew, so they called themselves Grecian. They profaned the sabbath and did not keep the feast days, just as our people profane today.

They had them “Set up altars, and groves, and chapels of idols, and sacrifice swine’s flesh”, and “leave their children uncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation”. This is the fullness of it: “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.” The goal was to make them forget the law. That is what Hellenized Jews have become today; they forgot the laws of God. This was us, Gentiles in times past, and it is what Paul was reminding them of.

This is the mission Esau set out to accomplish within our nation: to take away our heritage and make us something we are not. Look the word up, n-i-g-g-e-r: an inflammatory and deeply offensive racial slur, one of the most hateful epithets in the English language. Who called us that? The damn devil did. Hellenized Gentiles decided to flip it, put an a on the end, and call it a friendly or empowering term. There is nothing empowering about it. Your oppressor named you that to demean you, just as the Spaniards use their words for black; if they had only ever called us monkey, would we make that okay too? That is the mind of a Hellenized Jew, the same mind that went against the laws of God to live like the heathen and became the derogatory term their oppressors called them.

If you call a brother that, you are telling him he is unrepentant, that he fully learned the customs of the heathen and the Hellenization worked. That word is a mind frame. Brothers and sisters, we are not that, we have never been, and Lord's will we never will be again.

Paul deals with the same things in the different congregations, because the same things were happening in each place. “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”: remember back in the day, you were Gentiles, Hellenized Jews, Greeks.

“Who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands”. They were called Uncircumcision because their fathers in the time of the Maccabees decided they would not circumcise their children. The Circumcision in the flesh were those whose fathers stayed, who did not give up, who did not let their children be Hellenized. Paul is reminding them: you were living like heathens. It all says the same thing as 1 Corinthians 12:2.

Think about the mind frame of a person that followed idols. “What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?” Somebody formed the thing, then turned around and said this is God, this is what brought you out of Egypt. You have to be stupid to follow that.

“Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach!” Woe is destruction to the one who says that to a wooden idol. He is on a highway to hell, a fast track to destruction, following dumb idols that can do nothing for him. That is the mindset Paul is reminding the Corinthians they came out of.
“Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Stay the heck away from them. We came out of the dumb idols; we do not go back.

sense.text:
“Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord.” These are not common Hellenized words. An administration is the organisation, management and supervision of the daily operations of a body, coordinating people and resources to reach a goal. There are different administrations, different offices, all working toward the functioning and productivity of one body.

“And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all.” Operations are the inner workings, the behind-the-scenes processes that actually make the thing work. Different administrations and different operations, but they all work for the same thing.

Write it down: diversity does not mean division. Though an administration deals with something you do not deal with, it is not separate. And different roles do not mean inequality. No function, operation or administration can be looked on as unneeded; there is a reason it is there. The body is alive because these administrations and operations function. That is why you can walk, talk, fart, whatever you have to do: it all works hand in hand, even the uncomely things.

“But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” Everyone has a gift, going toward the same goal in unison. It is not just for you. However the manifestation comes, different gifts are given so that you can profit with all the nation.

“For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom”: the wise brothers who can show you something and tell you, do that and this is what will happen; no, do not do that. How many times have we gone against wisdom and found out the hard way? A hard head makes a soft behind. Gifts are given so that people can learn and listen.

“To another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit”: the same spirit that gave one man wisdom gave another knowledge. Not everybody is a concordance; some have to look it up, and some have that retention, a photographic memory, boom, boom, boom. That is a gift.

“To another faith by the same Spirit”. There are people in the body whose faith benefits you. When Bishop was going through his sickness, the word cancer was a fearful thing to a man who had lost his mother to it, and he was scared. Deacon Malachi looked without blinking and said, Do you think the Lord is going to let him go this way right now? Nah, brethren. Have faith. The spirit of faith was on Deacon Malachi, and it was given for the one who was afraid, so he could have that spirit too, keep praying and fasting, and not be around Bishop all doom and gloom. Spirits like that drag you down; we have to keep each other in check. The spirit of faith has been given to brothers and sisters in the body.

“To another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit”: all by the same spirit. We all have moments of weakness, and that is why we need each other, and leadership that is not scared to speak the truth.

The working of miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, divers kinds of tongues, the interpretation of tongues: all different offices and gifts the Lord gives throughout the body. “But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit”: all of them work together for one goal, one mission.

“Dividing to every man severally as he will.” God divided to every man as he wanted; everyone has received something. A new brother is trying to discover himself and figure out what the Lord wants him to do here. You woke up in this time period for a reason: what are you bringing to the table, how will you benefit your people, how will you carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same thing; this is about a nation, not just the brothers.

“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” Christ is the head and we, the church, are his body: many members, one body.

“For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body”. This is not talking about being dunked in water. Baptized means to cleanse; it does not automatically mean dipped in water. Strike that from your thoughts, the way a lot of Southern Baptists think.

“Whether we be Jews or Gentiles”: the Jews are the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin and Levi, and the Gentiles are the ten tribes of the northern kingdom. This is not Esau saying it is for him too. Northern or southern kingdom, all are one.

“Whether we be bond or free”: whether you were a bondman or a free man, for some purchased their freedom and some were in servitude, we all have a way back. “And have been all made to drink into one Spirit.” There is only one way to the kingdom, and that is the way we have been made to drink. Northern or southern kingdom, bond or free, we all partake of the same thing and all have access to the Lord.

precepts.why:
“For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. One body, but everybody does not do the exact same thing. Your whole function is not just camp, camp, camp. We are evolving, things are changing, and with the exponential growth Bishop spoke of comes responsibility and the organising of these different operations and administrations.

“So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.” Being many administrations, many operations, many different parts, we are one body in Christ.

“There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.” The diversities of gifts, administrations and operations all come back to one: one body, one spirit, one Lord, one God working in all.

“As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another”. The gift comes from the Lord, and it is for ministering one to another. You have not been given a gift just for you. If you have a gift and only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord. You are supposed to use it to benefit your nation and your people; that is why you were given it.

“As good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” This is why there is a stewardship programme: the gifts are to be used for the building of the body, so we can do what we need to do in this nation. If your gift only glorifies you, it is not about Christ; it is about you.

Some people have the gift of gab: brothers who can get a flyer into anybody's hand, even the man who walked off from you telling you to go screw yourself. You may have used a gift like that to hustle and get over on people in the world, but that is not why you were given it. Once your mind is renewed you understand God gave you that gift to get the word out, to relate to people and show them thus saith the Lord. If you are not using it for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you; Satan did. God gives gifts with purpose.

“Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” How can I apply this gift to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? What little brick can I put in that will bring us where we need to be? That is the mind frame of a body functioning as a whole. Paul had to tell them at the beginning: I cannot have you ignorant the way Hellenized Jews are ignorant.

“Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”: whatever gift the Lord gave you, give it with everything you have.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching”: everybody staying in his lane, working within the gift and skill set he has, not forcing things that are not him. Size is not everything: at camp you cannot put the 105-pound brother at the front sentry, for the wind will carry him away however much faith he has, but he might be a fire teacher or real good on flyers. When you are outside your character, things get messy, and when someone pretends to be what he is not and is put in a position, the one who should be there cannot operate the way the body needs and we lack.

Once a brother who was faithful and came early every sabbath was put over the bills, and one sabbath the lights were off at the school; he was not the one to put over the bills. Things were switched, and he is now operating in his proper place. Everybody does not belong everywhere.

“Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.” Everyone in his office, in his proper position.

God gives these different spirits. “See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah: And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship”. The Lord created him for this purpose and brought him to them.

“To devise cunning works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass”. Bezaleel probably thought he was just good at craftsmanship, at gold and metals. No: God gave him that talent for a purpose, and here he finds it out.

“And in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee”. God put it in them so that they could do it; that is why it was given. The tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the furniture, the candlestick, the altars, the laver, the holy garments, the anointing oil and the incense: “according to all that I have commanded thee shall they do.” They were given a gift from God so that all the Lord wanted could come to pass.

The Lord will send souls in so these things get accomplished. The congregation went from a fold-up table with a cloth on it to a wooden table and a stage, because the Lord brought brothers who could build. We cannot sit on people's talents, and you cannot sit on your hands. If you have been given a gift, use it, everything in its time and its order.

“But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.” He that descended into the lower parts of the earth ascended “far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.” Many do not understand what happened when Christ gave his life for the nation and what it opened for us. Christ spoke of the spiritual power that would go forth, and that is what has happened today: it is a miracle that we even know who we are. Our coming back to who we are shows the power of God.

“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”. He set up apostles within the body. Evangelists are those who go out and spread the word.

“For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ”. That is the function and purpose of the apostle, prophet, evangelist, pastor and teacher; this is why you were sent.

“Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. That perfect man is us coming into the fullness of the body, into what God created us to be: the body of Christ.

A precept for the body being one: “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you”. The many members speak the same thing, with no divisions, as one body.

“And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.” The whole body is knit together and nourished from the head, and so it grows with the increase of God.

“And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body”. All things are under Christ's feet. Who is the head? Christ. Who is the body? The church. And who is the church? Us.

“The fulness of him that filleth all in all.” So also is Christ: the one body with many members is the body of Christ.

Christ is the head of the body. “And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.” Christ is before all things, and the many members are one body under him.

This goes into wisdom, and into the gift, because the wisdom God gives comes through those gifts and the spirit he puts on you. “Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?” There is no profit in hiding the gift, or the administration God has set you in.

“Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.” A man that hides his folly is better than one who hides his wisdom and hoards up the understanding God has given him. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to push the truth and grow the unity God called us to, because we are all one body, all going to the same spirit. It all goes back to endeavouring to keep the unity.

“I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance”. If baptism always meant water, why would John need to say with water? Baptized means to cleanse: I indeed cleanse you with water unto repentance.

“But he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear”. John is letting you know water baptism was his administration, a tool he used to show forth repentance. Getting dunked was never a requirement for the kingdom. One was coming far mightier than he.

“He shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. Did you hear anything about water? No. The baptism we must come under is through Christ.

It says the same thing: “I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire”. This is not talking about water, in case somebody relapsed.

“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.” You want the baptism of the spirit. Fire is coming to clean up everything else; that is the judgment Christ is coming with.

“There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.” People pull this one without understanding what Paul is talking about, then sing and clap and try to talk over you so you cannot bring them back to what the Bible actually says. Many do not know what the ushering in of the Messiah brought, or why Christ was sent.

Neither Jew nor Greek is talking about the division between the southern and northern kingdoms, which Ezekiel 37 and Ephesians 2 make plain.

“Take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions”: Judah is the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin and Levi. “Then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”: the northern kingdom, Ephraim, Manasseh, Gad, Simeon, Naphtali, Asher, Reuben.

“And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.” Bring them back together: one nation, one body. The kingdom was split under Rehoboam, Solomon's son, and Jeroboam, when the northern kingdom said, See to thine own house.

“Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.” This is Christ doing it. Christ has the ability to make us one and is the one who will unite us.

“Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”, from among the Gentiles, the northern kingdom, “and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land”. That is the prophecy. “And I will make them one nation”: we were split in two, and he brings us back together, one nation, one fold, with “one king”, “neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” No more division. That is what neither Jew nor Greek means.

“Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols”: the northern kingdom was living in idolatry, like heathens, like Greeks, like the other nations. “But I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” It is speaking of a specific people.

sense.text:
Paul brings up the exact same thing as Ezekiel 37. None of us should ever get hemmed up on Paul's writings; give them the history and make them explain what they read. “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”: you were heathens, living like the Greeks and the nations around you.

The Circumcision called them Uncircumcision because historically, the way they were living, they did not circumcise their children. They did what the Grecians wanted and grew up under the customs of the heathen, so the Circumcision did not fool with them.

“That at that time ye were without Christ”: before you came unto repentance, you were without the Messiah, cast off. “Being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel”: the Jews had no dealings with them, no dealings with the Samaritans or the northern kingdom. “And strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world”: lost and hopeless before the Messiah came, living like heathens and following dumb idols.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Far off is where we were scattered, the islands of the sea, Pathros, Cush. Now you are made near, brought close.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one”. The both are the two sticks, Judah and Joseph, southern and northern kingdom. “And hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”: that partition was the hatred, the enmity, envy and vexation between the northern and southern kingdoms, and Christ is doing away with it.

“Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances”. When Christ gave his life he died for the whole nation and removed every excuse: my forefathers sacrificed here, my father had this land this long, who was first, who is supposed to be over what. The ordinances are the sacrifices, and that is how he ended the beef. All of it is out the window; you have to go through Christ. “For to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace”: that one new man is the body.

“And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross”. You cannot run from that word reconcile: to be reconciled, you had to once be together. At one time we were, then the split happened, the wall of partition was built, and it has not been right since. Now through Christ both have the opportunity to make it to the kingdom.

“Having slain the enmity thereby: And came and preached peace to you which were afar off, and to them that were nigh.” That is why Christ dealt with the Samaritan woman in John 4 and spoke to others of the northern kingdom. He understood his mission: the ushering in of the Messiah was for the unification of the body, bringing Israel back as one. Your forefathers were cut off, and now you must be brought back to who you are. You are not a Puerto Rican, not a Native American; you are an Israelite.
“For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.” Both the northern and the southern kingdom have access.

“Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners”. That is why we were called Gentiles: you were called a stranger and a foreigner because you were among them, living like them, and those who remained said, they are dead, they are done, when the Lord comes back they are finished, and cut you off. Now you are “fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”. That is what we now are. The Lord brought us back together: in this room the northern and southern kingdoms are together again, and that wall of partition is done.

precepts.why:
What the middle wall of partition looks like: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Has this happened yet? No; we are waiting on this second coming, to be delivered again.

Our people are in all those places, and we have to touch every one of them. That is why unification is so important. We have a lot of work to do.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts are those who were kept afar off, living among the other nations as heathens, the Hellenized Jews.

“The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” That envy is the wall of partition between us, and it is going to be gone. No more of this division: you light skinned, I am dark skinned, look at your hair, look at my hair. The northern kingdom was touched by Esau, the southern kingdom has had its dealings with the Nilotes too; we have all gone through changes and look different today, but we are all the same people. Christ is tearing that wall down.

sense.text:
“For the body is not one member, but many.” The foot that is not the hand, the ear that is not the eye, is still of the body. “If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing?” “But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.”

Name the functions of this body: security, the kitchen, medical, maintenance, AV, those who clean, hospitality, outreach, fundraising, the kids corner. The brothers wiping the doorknobs saved you from a whole heap of trouble you never thought about. The congregation takes the kids corner for granted until the kids are back out in the class. We have different offices that help this thing function, and everybody is important.

“And if they were all one member, where were the body? But now are they many members, yet but one body. And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.” Imagine one member telling another, your job ain't that important. Remove anything and we feel the change. Take the kitchen away and the sabbath feels completely different; let the bathrooms go down with maintenance nowhere to be found and people drive home from the sabbath. We need every portion.

“Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary”. The janitorial work seems feeble; the kids corner might seem like whatever, until it stops operating. Some offices never get seen, like whoever is back there hitting the buttons, yet the buttons bring clarity to the class. The brothers of the spirit sounding off when a point is made make a person really consider what was said, and it may stand out when he goes home. Nothing is small in this body; everything has a purpose.

“And our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.” The uncomely parts of the physical body, the pinky toe, even the booty hole: let that close down and you will die within a day or two. The uncomely parts are of the utmost importance, and we cannot look down on them, or they will feel they are not useful. Counsel given in secret, not for vain glory, is like that: it is never told to everybody, but it matters all the time.

“But God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked: That there should be no schism in the body”. The Lord tempered the body together. Are schisms going to happen anyway? Oh, yeah; they are promised to happen. Satan attacks unity, and whenever we are unified he will try to jump on somebody.

These are clear signs that a body is fractured or fracturing, from leadership down: constant murmuring; cliques forming, groups that do not want other people around, brothers who do not want to read the Bible with a certain brother; isolation, people distancing themselves; secret conversations and hidden discussions; prideful individualism, those who will not listen, have their own thoughts on how things are supposed to be and cannot be corrected; emotional decision making instead of doing it scripturally; lying or dealing falsely; and refusal to forgive, holding a grudge. That destroys the body. We have to forgive the way Christ told us to: husbands, wives, brothers, sisters, let it go.

The signs of a healthy body, fitly joined together: healthy communication; patience, members forbearing one another; forgiveness, not holding a thing over someone's head for the rest of his life; structured leadership; congregational support, showing up for a brother who needs help, as long as he gives us time; humility, which creates unity and builds faith. A humble teacher who does not know the answer says, I don't know, I have to look that up, instead of freestyling a breakdown and sending you home thinking you have understanding. A shared mission: a body that understands the goal is the strongest body you will have. And endurance through pressure, which reveals faith, strengthens unity and develops spiritual maturity. Those who have been through things and are still standing are seen; they are a rock, standing on Christ.

precepts.why:
If you think of yourself as better than somebody else, you are not in the spirit at all. “For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” To think soberly is to think with a clear mind, understanding that God has dealt severally to the body and that every single person matters.

Think like that and you will have more respect for every individual who walks through the door. You will not deal harshly with the people coming in or look down on them, because you started in the same place, maybe without a Bible or with the wrong Bible. It could be Daniel, Isaiah, Peter or James walking in on day one; would you treat them like crap? There is not one person better than the next. We all have an intricate part to play, so let us work together and make this thing great.

We have to work together. “Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.” When we work together there is reward, and the more of us there are, the more we can do. They look at us crazy because we filled a ship with hundreds of people and took the gospel to about eight countries without asking anybody's permission. Collectively, we are strong.

“For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.” In Oklahoma in 2006 there was only one, alone, and he had to leave and go where two are better than one to get built up, or he would have destroyed himself. There is strength in numbers: we hold each other accountable, support and look after each other, if we truly love the Lord. But if we come in like Hellenized Jews, the numbers will not profit us.

“Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” That is the humility we have to bring ourselves to in dealing with each other: prefer one another, and do nothing in strife or vain glory, for yourself or to glorify yourself. The reward is never of the Lord when you do it like that. From a collective stance it is so much better.

“These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.” There is a whole lot of pain and sorrow contained in this verse, yet Christ says he overcame the world. These things are going to happen no matter what, and in him we have peace.

If you think you have been through some things, get ready; the story is not over. “This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born upon the earth shall fight”: this is the reality we live in. Sorrow and travail, pain, tribulation, struggle, poverty and death wait for every man the moment he is born.

“That, if he be overcome, he shall suffer as thou hast said”: if you are overcome by all the world throws at you and give up in the day of adversity, you will suffer just as we have been told. “But if he get the victory, he shall receive the thing that I say”: endure to the end, keep fighting, never give in, keep endeavouring to keep the unity, and you receive the kingdom.

“For this is the life whereof Moses spake unto the people while he lived, saying, Choose thee life, that thou mayest live.” Everyone must fight this battle and everyone must choose. Ten years from now not everyone in this room will be here, and there will be a grand story why, but the truth is they did not want to fight; they gave up and let Satan overcome them. You can only speak for yourself: endure to the end.

Schisms are going to come and problems are going to happen; it is part of being in this truth. When you came in you caught hell: family, old contacts from years ago calling out of nowhere. Satan did not want to let you go.

“Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.” It is inevitable.

There are going to be schisms and divisions among us, all to find out who is built for the battle. Will a confrontation with a sister take you out? A marijuana addiction, women, porn? Or will you keep fighting and throwing blows back while you are getting hit? As long as you are fighting you are all right.

“For first of all, when ye come together in the church, I hear that there be divisions among you; and I partly believe it. For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” It has to happen. Everyone still sitting here made it through some trial. As Bishop said in San Diego, pressure either bursts pipes or what? Which one are you? Pressure exposes the weak points so you can see where the repairs need to be made, and it shows who is strong, like the sister who went through heavy things with her husband and is still here, who did not curse God and die. Never run from pressure or confrontation; these things have to happen so we can see clearly who is who.

“It is impossible but that offences will come”. You cannot stop it. In this truth somebody will disappoint you, misunderstand you, correct you, overlook you, frustrate you, and you will take a thing one way when it was meant another. The question is what you will do.

With your siblings you did not run away from home; you stayed and dealt with it, and you did not stop loving them, because they were family. It is the same here: hard, difficult, awkward times, but we are in the trenches and we are not leaving. I will correct you, and you had better correct me if I am wrong.

Satan attacks unity, and we are not ignorant of his devices: anything positive, he tries to come in and ruin, because he hates us unified. “And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.”

Imagine a body divided against itself, punching itself in the nose. An autoimmune disease is when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own healthy cells, tissues and organs. That is what we look like gnashing and biting against one another, working against each other and stepping over each other for rank, position, authority or pride. We are all the same, and Lord's will we will all be told, Job well done. Do not chase a bigger crown; just get in the door.
